### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6dd6a7d43e8fc5158a22941eefe0076fb856ef72` — the merge of head `bdb029939b57820bccfa2fb91ce59dcbb3303141` into base `24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6dd6a7d43e8fc5158a22941eefe0076fb856ef72 && git checkout 6dd6a7d43e8fc5158a22941eefe0076fb856ef72
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6 bdb029939b57820bccfa2fb91ce59dcbb3303141 && git checkout -B drift-repro 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6 && git merge --no-ff bdb029939b57820bccfa2fb91ce59dcbb3303141

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24f2f4014d0c9bbd43ec6928942fa44b21c1dff6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bdb029939b57820bccfa2fb91ce59dcbb3303141`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.page-record-no-component-refused.ts + none

PR #33315 · card #32759 · net diff against `main` (merge-base `fd7b378c`, `main` read at `24f2f401`): 2 files, the entry (+4 −2) and `.changeset/32759-page-record-no-component-entry-text.md` (+10). No file in the diff implements or enforces the entry, so the implementing set is `none`; the changeset is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** The diff replaces the tail of two string literals (`reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`) in one `SemanticMigration`. `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `conversionIds` (absent), the header comment and every schema, rule and runtime answer are byte-identical to `main`. No document parses differently.
- **Public surface: text only — right.** The entry's shape and id are unchanged; what moves is the prose `@objectstack/spec` ships in `dist` and projects into `spec-changes.json` and `protocol-upgrade-guide.md`.
- **Derived artifacts: nothing committed to regenerate — right.** `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`, `packages/spec/spec-changes.json`, `packages/spec/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` and `content/docs/protocol-upgrade/` are gitignored on `main` (`.gitignore` :68, :154, :155, :119) and none is tracked; the tracked `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` is a 15-line pointer that renders no entry text; `registry.ts.template` carries no fragment for this id. The gates that read the projection (`check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`) run in memory.
- **Pin tests: none reads this text — right.** The only test naming the id, `packages/spec/src/ui/page.test.ts` :1286–1290, asserts the entry exists and `conversionIds` is empty. The :1235 title "naming the blank panel and the fixes" pins the parse refusal's message (`RECORD_PAGE_PLACES_NO_COMPONENT`, `page.zod.ts`), which still says "blank detail panel"; it is correctly left alone.
- **Other tracked copies of the old sentence:** `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` :1171 (the 18.4.0 Unchanged bullet) still says "the console still draws the blank panel". It is release-owned (AGENTS.md, Documentation Guardrails) and correctly not touched here; the dev report carries it as an out-of-scope finding for the spec seat. `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx` :212 and :550 describe the two changes in the past tense and are not stale.
- **Runtime-string rule:** the new sentences carry no tracker number.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — correct. No accept set widens or narrows and no export moves. The changeset is `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, which matches what the diff publishes (corrected text in a released package, so a changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong). Both declaration lines (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`) are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body and agree. Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed; the entry is already registered and its id is unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the `os-dev-report` (comment 6880693638). Nothing to answer.
- Out-of-scope finding in the report (stale 18.4.0 CHANGELOG bullet): correctly routed, not ridden on this PR. It needs a card or a dedicated docs-only PR from the spec seat; the PR lands without it.
- Branch `claude/project-thread-wvx9ah` is not `claude/issue-32759-*`; claim 6880046730 declares why (thread-designated branch). Accepted as declared.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no author note owed.
- PR is a draft with no auto-merge armed.
- **Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-14T16:35Z, 44 runs:** no failure, no cancellation, no timed-out run. Completed: 14 success, 10 skipped (opt-in or event-gated jobs). Still `in_progress` (20) when this record was written: Build Core, Build UI Deps, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` are green. This PASS is the contract verdict; the all-green landing check stays the seat's to read once the pending runs conclude.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.page-record-no-component-refused.ts`, judged against the console on `main` (read, not reviewed): `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` :322–334 and :4558–4589, `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` :4031–4033, `ui/packages/react/src/hooks/usePageAssignment.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts` :1677–1763.

Sentence by sentence:

- "opening a record of its object in the console draws an explanation panel in place of the detail view" — holds. The branch `assignedPage && recordPagePlacesNoComponent(resolvedPage)` returns an `Empty` panel (`data-testid="record-page-places-no-component"`) instead of the page body, asks the spec's own `checkPageRecordPlacesComponent`, and by its comment never draws the default page in its place. The record drawer renders the same view, so "in the console" is not too wide.
- "naming the page" — holds for a stored row: the description interpolates `resolvedPage.name`; the unnamed variant only serves a row with no `name`, and `PageSchema.name` is required.
- "the three fixes: place components in a region, make the page kind slotted, or delete it" — holds, and in the panel's own order: "add components to a region, make the page slotted to show the default record page, or delete the page so the default record page shows". "Three" is the panel's count; the fourth route (name another type) lives in `replacement` and the parse refusal, and the sentence does not claim the panel names it.
- `acceptanceCriteria`, "not the explanation panel that names the page and its fixes" — holds: after any of the fixes the check no longer refuses, so the branch is not taken and the default page or the placed components draw.
- Sentences left unchanged — correct to leave. "opened every record of its object on a blank detail panel" is the pre-refusal history; "saying that every record would open on a blank panel" quotes the parse refusal, whose text on `main` still reads "would open on a blank detail panel".

Attempts to break it: a row that also carries off-spec `children` (same panel, since the check does not read `children`); a missing or unreadable record (that state shows first, and the sentence is conditioned on opening a record); the named page route (a refused name never reaches the branch, an accepted one does); a page that places a component, or a `slotted`, `html` or `react` page (not refused by the check, so not described by the sentence). None contradicts the text.

Findings:

- **F1 — nit (pre-existing reach, not introduced here).** The entry's surface counts a page with no `type` as a record page, and the spec check judges it so, but the console's selection (`isRecordPageOf`, `usePageAssignment.ts` :102–106) requires `type === 'record'` literally. A stored row whose body omits `type` would not be selected for its object unless it is served with the default filled in; then the record view draws the default page, not the panel. I did not establish which way stored bodies are served. The sentence this PR replaces had exactly the same reach ("draws the blank panel for its object"), so the diff neither introduces nor widens it. Disposition: accepted deviation here; worth a follow-up card to read how a no-`type` page row reaches `useMetadata().pages`.
- **F2 — nit.** The sentence speaks of "a page row already stored this way" only. The console draws the same panel for a page a package registers flat (the case the same `reason` says "installs as before"). True as written, slightly narrower than what the console does. Disposition: accepted deviation.

No must-fix, no should-fix. Nits only: the round ends.
